author: high6
claim: Let (G) be a finite connected undirected graph with at least one edge. Suppose every vertex of (G) has even degree. Prove that (G) has a closed trail that traverses every edge exactly once.

verification_report.summary: The proof is correct and complete. A maximum-length trail exists by finiteness and is shown to be closed using the parity of used and unused edge incidences at a hypothetical distinct terminal vertex. If an edge remained unused, connectedness would provide an unused edge incident with a vertex of the closed trail; cyclically reordering the trail to start at that vertex and appending the unused edge would contradict maximality. Thus the closed trail traverses every edge exactly once.

claim: Let (G) be a finite connected undirected graph with at least one edge. Suppose every vertex of (G) has even degree. Prove that (G) has a closed trail that traverses every edge exactly once.

verification_report.summary: The proof is correct. It first constructs a nonempty closed trail using finiteness and the even-degree parity argument, then chooses a closed trail with the maximum number of edges. If an edge were omitted, connectedness supplies a vertex of the maximal trail incident with a residual edge; deleting the trail leaves an even-degree residual graph, in which the same parity argument produces a nonempty closed trail that can be spliced into the maximal one. This contradiction shows that every edge is traversed exactly once. All hypotheses are used, and the proof contains no unsupported references or prohibited justification patterns.

verification_report.summary: The proof is correct and complete. A longest trail exists because the graph has finitely many edges and at least one edge. The parity argument correctly shows that such a longest trail must be closed: if its endpoints differed, the terminal vertex would have odd degree among used edges and hence a positive odd degree among unused edges, allowing extension. Connectivity then correctly ensures that if any edge were unused, some unused edge would be incident with a vertex of the closed trail; cyclically shifting the trail to start at that vertex and appending the unused edge would again contradict maximality. Thus the closed trail traverses every edge exactly once. All stated hypotheses are used, and no external references or prohibited citation patterns occur.
